sanskrit: tac chrutvā nipuṇaṃ sarvaṃ bharataḥ saha mantribhiḥ iṅgudīmūlam āgamya rāmaśayyām avekṣya tām
english: Having heard all of this in detail, Bharata, together with his ministers, came to the foot of the iṅgudī tree and beheld that bed of Rāma.

sanskrit: abravīj jananīḥ sarvā iha tena mahātmanā śarvarī śayitā bhūmāv idam asya vimarditam
english: He said to all his mothers: "Here on the ground that great-souled one spent the night sleeping; this grass has been pressed down by his body."

sanskrit: mahābhāgakulīnena mahābhāgena dhīmatā jāto daśarathenorvyāṃ na rāmaḥ svaptum arhati
english: "Rāma, born of the illustrious Daśaratha, himself supremely illustrious, high-born, and wise, does not deserve to sleep upon the bare earth."

sanskrit: ajinottarasaṃstīrṇe varāstaraṇasaṃcaye śayitvā puruṣavyāghraḥ kathaṃ śete mahītale
english: "How does this tiger among men, who once lay on beds heaped with the finest spreads and covered with deer-skins above, now sleep upon the ground?"

sanskrit: prāsādāgra vimāneṣu valabhīṣu ca sarvadā haimarājatabhaumeṣu varāstaraṇaśāliṣu
english: "Always in the upper chambers of palaces, in mansions and in pavilions adorned with gold, silver, and jewels, furnished with the finest coverings —"

sanskrit: puṣpasaṃcayacitreṣu candanāgarugandhiṣu pāṇḍurābhraprakāśeṣu śukasaṃgharuteṣu ca
english: "— in chambers beautiful with heaped flowers, fragrant with sandal and aguru, gleaming like white clouds, and echoing with the calls of flocks of parrots —"

sanskrit: gītavāditranirghoṣair varābharaṇaniḥsvanaiḥ mṛdaṅgavaraśabdaiś ca satataṃ pratibodhitaḥ
english: "— ever wakened by the sounds of singing and music, by the jingling of fine ornaments, and by the noble beating of mṛdaṅgas —"

sanskrit: bandibhir vanditaḥ kāle bahubhiḥ sūtamāgadhaiḥ gāthābhir anurūpābhiḥ stutibhiś ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: "— that scourge of foes, honoured in due time by bards, by many sūtas and māgadhas with fitting songs and hymns of praise —"

sanskrit: aśraddheyam idaṃ loke na satyaṃ pratibhāti mā muhyate khalu me bhāvaḥ svapno 'yam iti me matiḥ
english: "This is hard to believe in the world; it does not seem true to me. My mind is confused; I think this must be a dream."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ daivataṃ kiṃ cit kālena balavattaram yatra dāśarathī rāmo bhūmāv evaṃ śayīta saḥ
english: "Surely there is no divinity mightier than Time, since Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is brought to sleep upon the earth in this manner."

sanskrit: videharājasya sutā sītā ca priyadarśanā dayitā śayitā bhūmau snuṣā daśarathasya ca
english: "And Sītā, the lovely daughter of the king of Videha, beloved daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, has lain upon the ground here."

sanskrit: iyaṃ śayyā mama bhrātur idaṃ hi parivartitam sthaṇḍile kaṭhine sarvaṃ gātrair vimṛditaṃ tṛṇam
english: "This is my brother's bed; here on this hard and rough ground he turned about, and all this grass has been pressed flat by his limbs."

sanskrit: manye sābharaṇā suptā sītāsmiñ śayane tadā tatra tatra hi dṛśyante saktāḥ kanakabindavaḥ
english: "I think Sītā slept here wearing her ornaments, for here and there one can see scattered drops of gold still clinging to this spot."

sanskrit: uttarīyam ihāsaktaṃ suvyaktaṃ sītayā tadā tathā hy ete prakāśante saktāḥ kauśeyatantavaḥ
english: "Clearly an upper garment of Sītā was spread here then, for these silk threads are still clinging and gleaming in this place."

sanskrit: manye bhartuḥ sukhā śayyā yena bālā tapasvinī sukumārī satī duḥkhaṃ na vijānāti maithilī
english: "I think that the bed beside her husband was pleasant enough that the tender, chaste, and gentle Maithilī did not perceive the hardship."

sanskrit: sārvabhauma kule jātaḥ sarvalokasukhāvahaḥ sarvalokapriyaḥ tyaktvā rājyaṃ priyam anuttamam
english: "Born into a family of sovereigns of the whole earth, delight of all the world, beloved of all the world — he has abandoned his kingdom, his dearest and most excellent possession."

sanskrit: katham indīvaraśyāmo raktākṣaḥ priyadarśanaḥ sukhabhāgī ca duḥkhārhaḥ śayito bhuvi rāghavaḥ
english: "How does Rāghava — dark as a blue lotus, red-eyed, lovely to behold, and worthy of every comfort — lie here upon the earth, who deserves no hardship at all?"

sanskrit: siddhārthā khalu vaidehī patiṃ yānugatā vanam vayaṃ saṃśayitāḥ sarve hīnās tena mahātmanā
english: "The Vaidehi has truly achieved her purpose, having followed her husband into the forest; we are all left in uncertainty, bereft of that great-souled one."

sanskrit: akarṇadhārā pṛthivī śūnyeva pratibhāti mā gate daśarathe svarge rāme cāraṇyam āśrite
english: "With Daśaratha gone to heaven and Rāma retired to the forest, the earth appears to me like a rudderless ship, utterly empty."

sanskrit: na ca prārthayate kaś cin manasāpi vasuṃdharām vane 'pi vasatas tasya bāhuvīryābhirakṣitām
english: "No one, even in mind, craves this earth, which is protected by the power of his arms even while he dwells in the forest."

sanskrit: śūnyasaṃvaraṇārakṣām ayantritahayadvipām apāvṛtapuradvārāṃ rājadhanīm arakṣitām
english: "The royal capital is without guard at its enclosures, with horses and elephants unrestrained, with its city gates left open, and unprotected."

sanskrit: aprahṛṣṭabalāṃ nyūnāṃ viṣamasthām anāvṛtām śatravo nābhimanyante bhakṣyān viṣakṛtān iva
english: "Enemies do not covet it, with its joyless army, diminished, in an unstable state, and unprotected — just as they would not eat food laced with poison."

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti bhūmau tu śayiṣye 'haṃ tṛṇeṣu vā phalamūlāśano nityaṃ jaṭācīrāṇi dhārayan
english: "From this day forward I shall sleep on the ground or on grass, living constantly on fruits and roots, wearing matted hair and bark-cloth garments."

sanskrit: tasyārtham uttaraṃ kālaṃ nivatsyāmi sukhaṃ vane taṃ pratiśravam āmucya nāsya mithyā bhaviṣyati
english: "For his sake I shall dwell contentedly in the forest for the remaining time, taking upon myself that vow — it shall not prove false for him."

sanskrit: vasantaṃ bhrātur arthāya śatrughno mānuvatsyati lakṣmaṇena saha tv āryo ayodhyāṃ pālayiṣyati
english: "Śatrughna shall dwell here with me for my brother's benefit, while the noble one together with Lakṣmaṇa shall protect Ayodhyā."

sanskrit: abhiṣekṣyanti kākutstham ayodhyāyāṃ dvijātayaḥ api me devatāḥ kuryur imaṃ satyaṃ manoratham
english: "May the twice-born install Kākutstha on the throne in Ayodhyā — may the gods grant that this wish of mine be fulfilled."

sanskrit: prasādyamānaḥ śirasā mayā svayaṃ bahuprakāraṃ yadi na prapatsyate tato 'nuvatsyāmi cirāya rāghavaṃ vane vasan nārhati mām upekṣitum
english: "If, when I propitiate him myself with bowed head in many ways, he still will not relent, then I shall dwell with Rāghava in the forest forever — dwelling there, he has no right to disregard me."

sanskrit: vyuṣya rātriṃ tu tatraiva gaṅgākūle sa rāghavaḥ bharataḥ kālyam utthāya śatrughnam idam abravīt
english: Having spent the night right there on the bank of the Gaṅgā, that Rāghava Bharata rose at dawn and spoke thus to Śatrughna:

sanskrit: śatrughottiṣṭha kiṃ śeṣe niṣādādhipatiṃ guham śīghram ānaya bhadraṃ te tārayiṣyati vāhinīm
english: "Rise, Śatrughna — why do you still sleep? Bring quickly the lord of the Niṣādas, Guha — good fortune to you — he shall ferry the army across."

sanskrit: jāgarmi nāhaṃ svapimi tathaivāryaṃ vicintayan ity evam abravīd bhrātrā śatrughno 'pi pracoditaḥ
english: "I am awake, not sleeping — I am thinking of our noble brother all the while" — thus spoke Śatrughna, urged by his brother.

sanskrit: iti saṃvadator evam anyonyaṃ narasiṃhayoḥ āgamya prāñjaliḥ kāle guho bharatam abravīt
english: While those two lions among men were conversing thus with each other, Guha arrived at the proper time, with hands folded, and addressed Bharata:

sanskrit: kaccit sukhaṃ nadītīre 'vātsīḥ kākutstha śarvarīm kaccic ca saha sainyasya tava sarvam anāmayam
english: "Did you pass the night comfortably on the river-bank, O Kākutstha? And is all well with your army?"

sanskrit: guhasya tat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā snehād udīritam rāmasyānuvaśo vākyaṃ bharato 'pīdam abravīt
english: Hearing those words of Guha, spoken out of affection, Bharata, who was fully under Rāma's sway, spoke in return:

sanskrit: sukhā naḥ śarvarī rājan pūjitāś cāpi te vayam gaṅgāṃ tu naubhir bahvībhir dāśāḥ saṃtārayantu naḥ
english: "Our night was comfortable, O king, and you have honoured us well. Now let your boatmen ferry us across the Gaṅgā with many boats."

sanskrit: tato guhaḥ saṃtvaritaḥ śrutvā bharataśāsanam pratipraviśya nagaraṃ taṃ jñātijanam abravīt
english: Then Guha, hastened by hearing Bharata's command, re-entered the town and spoke to those kinsmen of his:

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhata prabudhyadhvaṃ bhadram astu hi vaḥ sadā nāvaḥ samanukarṣadhvaṃ tārayiṣyāma vāhinīm
english: "Rise up, awaken — may good fortune always attend you! Draw the boats forth; we shall ferry the army across."

sanskrit: te tathoktāḥ samutthāya tvaritā rājaśāsanāt pañca nāvāṃ śatāny eva samāninyuḥ samantataḥ
english: Thus commanded, they rose up quickly at the king's order and assembled five hundred boats from all sides.

sanskrit: anyāḥ svastikavijñeyā mahāghaṇḍā dharā varāḥ śobhamānāḥ patākinyo yuktavātāḥ susaṃhatāḥ
english: Other boats, recognizable by auspicious marks, large and carrying great loads, fine vessels adorned with flags, fitted with sails, and firmly constructed, gleamed there.

sanskrit: tataḥ svastikavijñeyāṃ pāṇḍukambalasaṃvṛtām sanandighoṣāṃ kalyāṇīṃ guho nāvam upāharat
english: Then Guha brought forward a fine boat recognizable by auspicious marks, covered with white blankets, resounding with the noise of bells, and auspicious in every way.

sanskrit: tām āruroha bharataḥ śatrughnaś ca mahābalaḥ kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāś cānyā rājayoṣitaḥ
english: Bharata boarded that boat, and the mighty Śatrughna, and Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and the other royal wives.

sanskrit: purohitaś ca tat pūrvaṃ gurave brāhmaṇāś ca ye anantaraṃ rājadārās tathaiva śakaṭāpaṇāḥ
english: The purohita went first, then the brāhmaṇas who served as preceptors; immediately after them the royal women, and then the carts and the market-wagons.

sanskrit: āvāsam ādīpayatāṃ tīrthaṃ cāpy avagāhatām bhāṇḍāni cādadānānāṃ ghoṣas tridivam aspṛśat
english: The noise of those who were lighting the camp-fires, of those plunging into the ford, and of those loading the goods and equipment rose up and touched the heavens.

sanskrit: patākinyas tu tā nāvaḥ svayaṃ dāśair adhiṣṭhitāḥ vahantyo janam ārūḍhaṃ tadā saṃpetur āśugāḥ
english: Those flag-bearing boats, manned by the boatmen themselves, carrying the people who had boarded them, then shot swiftly across.

sanskrit: nārīṇām abhipūrṇās tu kāś cit kāś cit tu vājinām kaś cit tatra vahanti sma yānayugyaṃ mahādhanam
english: Some boats were filled with women, others with horses; and some there carried vehicles with their teams and great stores of wealth.

sanskrit: tāḥ sma gatvā paraṃ tīram avaropya ca taṃ janam nivṛttāḥ kāṇḍacitrāṇi kriyante dāśabandhubhiḥ
english: Having reached the far bank and disembarked the people, they returned; and the kinsmen of the boatmen busied themselves with various tasks.

sanskrit: savaijayantās tu gajā gajārohaiḥ pracoditāḥ tarantaḥ sma prakāśante sadhvajā iva parvatāḥ
english: The elephants, bearing their victory-banners and urged on by their mahouts, shone as they swam across like mountains adorned with flags.

sanskrit: nāvaś cāruruhus tv anye plavais terus tathāpare anye kumbhaghaṭais terur anye teruś ca bāhubhiḥ
english: Some others boarded boats to cross; yet others crossed on rafts; still others crossed using pots and water-jars as floats; and others crossed by the strength of their arms alone.

sanskrit: sā puṇyā dhvajinī gaṅgāṃ dāśaiḥ saṃtāritā svayam maitre muhūrte prayayau prayāgavanam uttamam
english: That sacred army, ferried across the Gaṅgā by the boatmen themselves, set out in the auspicious hour of Maitra toward the excellent forest of Prayāga.

sanskrit: āśvāsayitvā ca camūṃ mahātmā niveśayitvā ca yathopajoṣam draṣṭuṃ bharadvājam ṛṣipravaryam ṛtvig vṛtaḥ san bharataḥ pratasthe
english: Having reassured the army and settled it in camp as was fitting, the great-souled Bharata, accompanied by his priests, set forth to visit Bharadvāja, the foremost of seers.

sanskrit: bharadvājāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā krośād eva nararṣabhaḥ balaṃ sarvam avasthāpya jagāma saha mantribhiḥ
english: Catching sight of the hermitage of Bharadvāja from a distance of a krośa, that bull among men halted his entire army and went forward with his ministers alone.

sanskrit: padbhyām eva hi dharmajño nyastaśastraparicchadaḥ vasāno vāsasī kṣaume purodhāya purohitam
english: For that knower of dharma went on foot, having laid aside his weapons and equipment, dressed in two garments of fine linen, placing the purohita before him.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdarśane tasya bharadvājasya rāghavaḥ mantriṇas tān avasthāpya jagāmānu purohitam
english: Then, approaching the presence of Bharadvāja, that Rāghava left his ministers behind and followed after the purohita.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭham atha dṛṣṭvaiva bharadvājo mahātapāḥ saṃcacālāsanāt tūrṇaṃ śiṣyān arghyam iti bruvan
english: Then, seeing Vasiṣṭha, the great ascetic Bharadvāja quickly rose from his seat, instructing his disciples with the word "arghya — the water of welcome."

sanskrit: samāgamya vasiṣṭhena bharatenābhivāditaḥ abudhyata mahātejāḥ sutaṃ daśarathasya tam
english: Meeting with Vasiṣṭha and greeted reverentially by Bharata, that greatly resplendent sage recognized him as the son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: tābhyām arghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca dattvā paścāt phalāni ca ānupūrvyāc ca dharmajñaḥ papraccha kuśalaṃ kule
english: Having offered arghya and water for the feet to both, and fruits afterward, that knower of dharma inquired in due order about the welfare of their family.

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāṃ bale kośe mitreṣv api ca mantriṣu jānan daśarathaṃ vṛttaṃ na rājānam udāharat
english: He asked after Ayodhyā, after the army, the treasury, the allies, and the ministers; knowing what had befallen Daśaratha, he did not mention the king.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho bharataś cainaṃ papracchatur anāmayam śarīre 'gniṣu vṛkṣeṣu śiṣyeṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu
english: Vasiṣṭha and Bharata in turn asked him about his well-being — about his body, his sacred fires, the trees, his disciples, the deer, and the birds.

sanskrit: tatheti ca pratijñāya bharadvājo mahātapāḥ bharataṃ pratyuvācedaṃ rāghavasnehabandhanāt
english: Affirming that all was well, the great ascetic Bharadvāja then addressed Bharata thus, bound as he was by his affection for Rāghava:

sanskrit: kim ihāgamane kāryaṃ tava rājyaṃ praśāsataḥ etad ācakṣva me sarvaṃ na hi me śudhyate manaḥ
english: "What business brings you here, you who are the ruler of a kingdom? Tell me everything — for my mind does not feel at ease."

sanskrit: suṣuve yama mitraghnaṃ kausalyānandavardhanam bhrātrā saha sabhāryo yaś ciraṃ pravrājito vanam
english: "She bore one who destroys enemies and increases the joy of Kausalyā — he who has been sent long into the forest along with his wife and brother."

sanskrit: niyuktaḥ strīniyuktena pitrā yo 'sau mahāyaśāḥ vanavāsī bhavetīha samāḥ kila caturdaśa
english: "He of great renown was ordered by a father swayed by a woman to live in the forest for fourteen years."

sanskrit: kaccin na tasyāpāpasya pāpaṃ kartum ihecchasi akaṇṭakaṃ bhoktumanā rājyaṃ tasyānujasya ca
english: "Do you perhaps wish to do harm to that sinless one? Do you desire to enjoy undisputed sovereignty, yours and that of his younger brother?"

sanskrit: evam ukto bharadvājaṃ bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha paryaśru nayano duḥkhād vācā saṃsajjamānayā
english: Thus addressed, Bharata replied to Bharadvāja, his eyes overflowing with tears of grief, his voice faltering:

sanskrit: hato 'smi yadi mām evaṃ bhagavān api manyate matto na doṣam āśaṅker naivaṃ mām anuśādhi hi
english: "I am destroyed if even the venerable one thinks of me in this way. Let him not suspect any fault in me — please do not instruct me thus."

sanskrit: na caitad iṣṭaṃ mātā me yad avocan madantare nāham etena tuṣṭaś ca na tad vacanam ādade
english: "What my mother said in my absence is not something I wished for; I am not pleased by it, and I do not accept that word of hers."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu taṃ naravyāghram upayātaḥ prasādakaḥ pratinetum ayodhyāṃ ca pādau tasyābhivanditum
english: "But I have come here as a supplicant to that tiger among men, to bring him back to Ayodhyā and to prostrate myself at his feet."

sanskrit: tvaṃ mām evaṃgataṃ matvā prasādaṃ kartum arhasi śaṃsa me bhagavan rāmaḥ kva saṃprati mahīpatiḥ
english: "Knowing me to be thus disposed, you ought to show me your grace. Tell me, O venerable one — where is Rāma, the lord of the earth, now?"

sanskrit: uvāca taṃ bharadvājaḥ prasādād bharataṃ vacaḥ tvayy etat puruṣavyāghra yuktaṃ rāghavavaṃśaje guruvṛttir damaś caiva sādhūnāṃ cānuyāyitā
english: Bharadvāja, with kindness, spoke these words to Bharata: "In you, O tiger among men, born of the Rāghava lineage, this is fitting — reverence toward one's guru, self-restraint, and the following of the virtuous."

sanskrit: jāne caitan manaḥsthaṃ te dṛḍhīkaraṇam astv iti apṛcchaṃ tvāṃ tavātyarthaṃ kīrtiṃ samabhivardhayan
english: "I knew this already, that it was established in your heart — I asked you merely to confirm it, to magnify greatly your glory."

sanskrit: asau vasati te bhrātā citrakūṭe mahāgirau śvas tu gantāsi taṃ deśaṃ vasādya saha mantribhiḥ etaṃ me kuru suprājña kāmaṃ kāmārthakovida
english: "Your brother dwells on the great mountain Citrakūṭa; you shall go to that place tomorrow — tonight stay here with your ministers. Grant me this wish, O most wise one, O you who are skilled in the objects of desire."

sanskrit: tatas tathety evam udāradarśanaḥ pratītarūpo bharato 'bravīd vacaḥ cakāra buddhiṃ ca tadā mahāśrame niśānivāsāya narādhipātmajaḥ
english: Then that noble-visaged Bharata, of distinguished bearing, spoke the word "So be it," and the son of the lord of men resolved in his mind to spend the night in that great hermitage.
